PRACTICAL_LABS.title: Docker Compose Local AI Stack
PRACTICAL_LABS.setup: Docker Desktop or Docker Engine with Compose
PRACTICAL_LABS.code:
services:
  api:
    build: .
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://app:app@postgres:5432/app
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
      OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: ai-api
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    depends_on:
      - postgres
      - redis
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: app
      POSTGRES_DB: app
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
PRACTICAL_LABS.outcome: The local stack provides an API, durable relational state, cache/queue support, and a place to add tracing.

RISK_TRADEOFFS: Vendor SDK lock-in
Hosted providers are fast to production but can limit portability.
Use a gateway, typed adapter, provider-independent evals, and a fallback plan.
Legacy agent abstractions
Over-abstracted loops are difficult to debug and test.
Prefer explicit state, events, and bounded transitions.
Framework selection
Crew-style workflows are clear but can be less flexible for dynamic control.
Choose based on state complexity, observability, and team familiarity.
Fine-tuning cost
Adapters reduce cost but still require quality data and GPU access.
Try retrieval, prompt changes, or tool design before fine-tuning.
Observability gaps
Without traces and evals, failures look like random model behavior.
Instrument prompts, retrieval, tools, latency, tokens, cost, and outcomes from day one.
MCP adoption
Protocol ecosystems evolve and servers may vary in quality.
Validate schemas, use allowlists, isolate credentials, and keep a fallback integration.
Context overflow
Dumping full documents or tool payloads degrades reasoning.
Persist artifacts, retrieve slices, summarize deliberately, and cap context.
Autonomy risk
Unbounded agent actions can create security, cost, or operational incidents.
Use least privilege, approvals, budgets, sandboxing, and rollback.
